subject: Post-call: routing & mode checklist for low-latency checkout
messages:
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: elliot.price@quickledger.com, lina.santos@quickledger.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: routing & mode checklist for low-latency checkout

Hi Elliot / Lina —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a lightweight checklist so we can recommend a pilot configuration that will validate whether Hosted API or Dedicated capacity is the right fit for QuickLedger’s checkout path.

Key notes from today’s discussion:
- Traffic shape: expected baseline ~25–40 QPS during business hours, with scheduled marketing spikes up to ~400 QPS for ~1–3 hour windows (once per week).
- Latency targets: p50 ~<100ms, p95 <250ms, p99 ideally <350–400ms for the token-generation portion of the pipeline.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; customer data residency US; no air-gapped requirement for now.
- Failure tolerance: checkout must not exceed 2–3s end-to-end on 99.9% of requests; graceful degradation acceptable (shorter summaries / model fallback).

What we need from your side to finalize the pilot URL and test plan:
1) A 7-day sample of production traffic profile (per-minute QPS bucketed by endpoint) or a short synthetic QPS schedule if you can’t share logs.
2) Representative prompt sizes (avg tokens in, avg tokens out) and typical max sequence length during checkout validation.
3) Confirmation if the spikes are predictable/scheduled (marketing) vs. unpredictable organic traffic.

Preliminary Redwood recommendation (based on today's data):
- Start with a Hosted API pilot configured with a 2-week burst policy (auto-burst to reserved instances during scheduled spikes) and continuous KV-prefetching for prefix-heavy calls. This lets us validate p99 tail behavior with real traffic without a long-term capacity commit.
- If sustained nightly throughput >150 QPS for more than 24h over the pilot, we recommend switching to a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for cost predictability and lower tail latency.
- If you later need on-prem or VPC isolation for production, we can transition the same model versions and rollout policy to Private with minimal config changes.

Attached: pilot_config.yaml (proposed target qps, test endpoints) and a short SLA chart that maps p99 latency to deployment modes.

Next steps / asks (can we get these by Tue 19 Mar?):
- Per-minute traffic sample or synthetic profile (see item #1)
- A short note from Procurement with preferred pilot SOW terms so Ben can draft a pilot quote
- A 60–90 minute window next week for a targeted benchmark run (we’ll need a stable test key and an agreed synthetic QPS ramp)

Cheers,
Connor O’Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0117

Attachments: pilot_config.yaml (text), redwood_sla_chart.pdf (pdf)

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and the traffic file attached (synthetic profile exported as CSV):

- Traffic: the large spikes are scheduled (marketing pushes) but timing varies by region; spikes last 1–3 hours and we see them ~1x per week on average.
- Token sizes: avg prompt 60 tokens, avg response 28 tokens; max conversation window we sometimes send is ~512 tokens.
- Baseline: nightly processing window averages 20–35 QPS; peak concurrent users map to the 400 QPS figure.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is in place; we will want KMS integration in production but not required for pilot.

I've attached the synthetic QPS profile as requested and included our procurement alias on the thread. Procurement will need a short SOW and a price cap for the pilot. Also looping in Lina (engineering) — she’s the point for the benchmark run.

Let us know your proposed pilot ramp schedule and any special headers or test tokens we should use.

—Elliot

Thanks Elliot — good data. Quick internal + external plan:

Internal note (to Connor/Marissa):
- I recommend we offer a 3-week Hosted pilot with the following constraints:
  * Week 1: baseline validation at nominal QPS (20–40) to confirm p50/p95 behavior and KV cache effectiveness.
  * Week 2: scheduled spike test (we simulate 400 QPS for a 2-hour window) and measure p99 tail and model fallbacks. We’ll enable burst reservations for that window to validate cost/latency trade-offs.
  * Week 3: optional extended test or cutover to a Dedicated pool if p99 remains >350ms during Week 2 sustained load.
- Pricing: pilot capped at $X,XXX (Ben will fill exact pilot quote once Procurement confirms SOW items).
- Success criteria: p95 <250ms and p99 <350ms during controlled spike; graceful-fallback percentage <2%.

To QuickLedger:
Connor and I can own scheduling the benchmark. Proposed slots: Tue 19 Mar 09:00–11:00 PT (ramp test) or Thu 21 Mar 14:00–16:00 PT. Are either of those good?

Connor — I’ll draft a short SOW and a one-page quote for Procurement. Marissa, can you confirm whether we need an on-call infra engineer for the scheduled spike night?

Forwarding final ops note — Elliot / Lina: we’re aligned on the pilot plan. Two quick operational asks before we book the ramp test:

1) Procurement: can you provide a PO or a signed short SOW template with a $X,XXX pilot cap? We can start running tests without a PO, but we require a signed SOW to enable reserved burst capacity.
2) Engineering: please confirm a test key and a stable test endpoint. For the ramp we prefer a single endpoint behind your checkout validation so we can isolate network variance.

We’ll run the bench from Redwood’s Hosted control plane and provide a detailed telemetry export (per-token latencies) after each test. If the spike test shows sustained p99 >350ms, we’ll present a cost/latency estimate for Dedicated (reserved) capacity and a migration plan.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call to review the SOW draft prior to signature.
